newsitem.title: UK: England, Wales farm grain stocks at record high.
newsitem.headline: England, Wales farm grain stocks at record high.

text.p: England and Wales had the largest ever end of season stocks of wheat and barley when the 1996-97 year finished at the end of June, according to the Home Grown Cereals Authority.
There were 930,000 tonnes of wheat and 150,000 tonnes of barley on farms, the HGCA said, quoting farm ministry figures.
There were 750,000 tonnes of wheat and 130,000 tonnes of barley held on farms a year earlier. These levels were also "considerably larger than usual," the HGCA said.

"Part of this increase can be accounted for by increasing domestic cereal consumption and the later harvest, both factors which tend to increase usage of such stocks before new crop becomes available," the HGCA said in its "Weekly Digest."
"However, the bulk of this extra on-farm stock will compete with new crop supplies for markets."
Closing stocks held by millers, feed compounders and merchants and ports are similar to previous seasons, the HGCA said.
"The prospect of these consumers taking more cereals from farms in the run-up to harvest can thus be largely discounted."
The large on-farm stocks were despite a rise in exports in 1996-97 of 38 percent for wheat and 63 percent for barley.
"The implications of the large end season stock levels very much depend on the size of the 1997 cereal harvest," the HGCA said.

"They will certainly add to new crop supplies, but if the crop is smaller than last season (as many industry sources are now suggesting) and exports remain strong then the extra carry-in may be easily absorbed.
